name: vwap_reclaim_trend_001
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the index has been trading below session VWAP for most of a 3-minute window, every VWAP-benchmarked institutional algorithm is accumulating passively at better-than-benchmark prices. The moment price reclaims VWAP with the 3-minute EMA crossing back above the 15-minute EMA, those accumulated long positions shift from passive absorption to active continuation — algo systems now need to fill the remainder of their order at or above VWAP, creating a 20-35 spot point continuation burst over the next 30-90 seconds. The bearish mirror applies when sustained above-VWAP drift reverses through VWAP with EMA structure turning negative, as benchmark algos unwind longs and delta-hedging flows accelerate the move.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: VWAP() = cumsum(typical_price * volume) / cumsum(volume), reset each session
indicators.purpose: Cumulative session VWAP — no scaling needed. It's a fixed-start-of-session anchor regardless of bar size. Same concept as original but now computed on 5s bars, giving finer resolution of the reclaim level.

indicators.name: below_vwap_count_36
indicators.purpose: 36 bars = 3 minutes. Original used 6-of-8 (75%) at 1-min = 6 minutes of dislocation required. At 5s scale we're holding 15-90 seconds so we want the dislocation to be meaningful but recent. 3 minutes captures enough context without looking too far back for a 30-90s trade. 75% threshold preserved.

indicators.name: above_vwap_count_36
indicators.purpose: Mirror of below_vwap_count_36 for bearish breakdown entries.

indicators.name: ema_fast
indicators.purpose: 3-minute EMA. Original used EMA(9) at 1-min = 9-min. Compressed to 3-min because at 5s scale we are trading the FAST leg of the reclaim, not the slow recovery. EMA(36) responds in seconds, confirming the immediate directional shift.

indicators.name: ema_slow
indicators.purpose: 15-minute EMA. Original used EMA(21) at 1-min = 21-min. Kept near this timeframe (15 vs 21 min) as session trend context filter. At 5s, this is 180 bars — broad enough to reflect the intraday institutional trend direction without lagging too much.

conditions: below_vwap_count_36 >= 0.75 * 36 (i.e., >= 27): NIFTY below VWAP for 75%+ of last 3 min
current close crosses above vwap (prev_close < vwap AND close >= vwap)
ema_fast > ema_slow: 3-min EMA above 15-min EMA confirms bullish structure
buy_ce.confirmation: Actual VWAP cross (prev bar below, current bar above) — filters premature entries mid-dislocation

conditions: above_vwap_count_36 >= 27: NIFTY above VWAP for 75%+ of last 3 min
current close crosses below vwap (prev_close > vwap AND close <= vwap)
ema_fast < ema_slow: 3-min EMA below 15-min EMA confirms bearish structure

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 spot points. A genuine VWAP reclaim on NIFTY should not retrace 8 spot points back through VWAP within seconds — if it does, the reclaim failed and accumulated longs are dumping. At delta ~0.5, 8 spot pts = 4 option pts; this is the minimum adverse move that unambiguously invalidates the thesis.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 spot points. VWAP reclaim continuations on NIFTY — where algo buyers switch from passive to active — typically carry 20-35 spot points in the first 60-90 seconds. 14 spot pts captures the conservative lower end (40-50% of the move), giving 1:1.75 R:R.

filters.vix_filter: none — VWAP reclaim works across VIX regimes since the mechanism is institutional benchmark flow, not sentiment
filters.time_filter: 09:35-13:30 IST — avoids opening range noise and afternoon choppy session when VWAP reclaims are less trustworthy
filters.volume_filter: implicit — NIFTY index volume is always sufficient; no additional volume gate needed
filters.trend_filter: EMA alignment (ema_fast vs ema_slow) serves as the trend structure filter
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — EMA/VWAP reclaim is well-known; crowding risk on obvious setups

adaptation_notes: Original traded Nifty200 stocks at 1-min on 8-24 bar holds with relative volume filter and ADX. Key changes: (1) Universe is now NIFTY index — no stock selection needed. (2) Relative volume filter dropped — NIFTY index volume is structurally sufficient and noisier at 5s; replaced by EMA alignment as the trend filter. (3) ADX replaced by EMA_fast vs EMA_slow crossover structure — ADX at 5s is too noisy; EMA alignment gives cleaner directional bias. (4) Dislocation window: 6-of-8 1-min bars → 27-of-36 5s bars (same 75% threshold, compressed to 3 min because we trade the fast reclaim leg). (5) ATR-based stop dropped — replaced by fixed option premium points calibrated to NIFTY's typical 30-90s spot move range.
weaknesses: VWAP reclaim signals are most common in morning session (09:35-11:30); afternoon reclaims post-13:00 are less reliable
On trend days when NIFTY spends most of the session above or below VWAP, there are few reclaim opportunities
EMA crossover confirmation adds lag — in fast-moving markets the entry may be late by 15-30 seconds
